title: Other AWS Database Services
description: Explore ElastiCache, MemoryDB, Neptune, DocumentDB, Keyspaces, and Timestream to choose the right specialized database for your workload.

data.text: AWS offers more than just RDS and DynamoDB. Specialized databases like ElastiCache for caching, Neptune for graphs, and Timestream for time series data let you pick the right tool for each job.
In-memory databases keep data in RAM instead of on disk, giving you microsecond response times. AWS offers two in-memory database services.

data.title: Amazon ElastiCache and MemoryDB
items: **Amazon ElastiCache** — managed Redis or Memcached for caching, session storage, and leaderboards. Data is in memory but not persisted by default.
**Amazon MemoryDB for Redis** — Redis-compatible in-memory database with durability. Unlike ElastiCache, MemoryDB persists data to disk for durability.

data.text: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service. It is designed for applications that need to navigate highly connected datasets, such as social networks, fraud detection, and recommendation engines. Neptune supports both property graph and RDF graph models.

data.title: Document and Wide-Column Databases
items: **Amazon DocumentDB** — a fully managed document database that is compatible with MongoDB. It is ideal for content management, catalogs, and user profiles stored as JSON-like documents.
**Amazon Keyspaces** — a fully managed wide-column database compatible with Apache Cassandra. It is great for high-throughput, low-latency workloads with a flexible schema.

data.text: Amazon Timestream is a fully managed time series database. It is optimized for IoT metrics, application logs, and operational data where you need to ingest, store, and query trillions of events per day. Timestream automatically tiers data between memory and disk to keep costs low.

data.title: AWS Database Services at a Glance

cards.title: ElastiCache
cards.description: In-memory caching with Redis or Memcached for fast lookups.
pros: Easy to add to existing apps
cons: Data lost if node fails (no persistence by default)

cards.title: Neptune
cards.description: Graph database for connected data like social networks and recommendation engines.

cards.title: DocumentDB
cards.description: MongoDB-compatible document database for JSON-like data.

cards.title: Keyspaces
cards.description: Managed wide-column database compatible with Apache Cassandra.

cards.title: Timestream
cards.description: Managed time series database for IoT and metrics data.
cons: Only for time series use cases

data.title: Choosing the Right Database
data.text: Use RDS or Aurora for relational data. Use DynamoDB for key-value or document workloads. Use ElastiCache for caching. Use Neptune for graphs. Use Timestream for time series. Use DocumentDB or Keyspaces for specialized NoSQL patterns.

data.title: Match Database to Use Case
data.description: Match each workload to the best AWS database service.
steps: A social network that needs to recommend friends of friends
A real-time leaderboard for a mobile game
A fleet of IoT sensors sending temperature readings every second
A product catalog with flexible attributes per category
data.expectedOutcome: You should match: graph queries → Neptune, leaderboard → ElastiCache/MemoryDB, IoT metrics → Timestream, product catalog → DocumentDB or DynamoDB.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ElastiCache provides in-memory caching; MemoryDB adds durability
Neptune is the graph database for highly connected data
DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible; Keyspaces is Cassandra-compatible
Timestream is purpose-built for time series and IoT data
data.takeaway: AWS has a database for every workload. Picking the right one saves money and improves performance.
